sources.label: Perseus canonical Latin literature
sources.note: Caesar, Bellum Gallicum: the Latin and the English XML of phi0448.phi001. The Greek side lives in the canonical-greekLit repo and joins the codex in the same folder when a game entry needs it.

sources.label: Project Gutenberg plain text
sources.note: About 1 MB per book. The plan also lists Pliny's Natural History volumes; their ebook ids are not in docs/plan/rome-codex.md, so they are added here as they are confirmed against the site.

sources.label: Wikipedia article list of the Roman army categories
sources.note: Each answer lists the member articles (88 and 77 in the plan). One member summary is https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/summary/<title>, fetched with the same rate limit as the member title is added to the table.

sources.label: Wikidata query of the Roman legions and their places

items.id: SELECT ?legion ?legionLabel ?place ?placeLabel ?coord WHERE { ?legion wdt:P31 wd:Q11303 . OPTIONAL { ?legion wdt:P276 ?place . } OPTIONAL { ?legion wdt:P625 ?coord . } SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". } }
items.name: legions-and-places.json

sources.note: One query every 60 s, as the plan states. The query text is url encoded into the sparql url.

sources.label: Pleiades ancient world places
sources.note: The place ids of the map (pleiades:423025 and friends) come from this dump. The gz stays gz: the loader gunzips it.

sources.label: Itiner-e Roman road network
sources.note: 78 MB of Roman roads, the biggest single pull of the codex. March time on a road comes from this file.

sources.label: Met Museum open access object list
sources.note: The Met retired its search api in 2024 (it answers 410 now), so the list comes from the open access csv on github, 340 MB with the lfs media url. The one object api, https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/{id}, still answers and is the second form once the csv names the ids.

sources.label: Art Institute of Chicago open access search
sources.note: The search answer holds the artwork ids and the IIIF image ids. The image itself is https://www.artic.edu/iiif/2/<image_id>/full/843,/0/default.jpg.

sources.label: Wikimedia Commons Trajan's Column files
sources.licence: per file, as the file page states
sources.note: About 280 files in the category. The answer holds every file url and its licence string, so the reference boards can point at the file and the licence together.

sources.label: Poly Haven texture list
sources.note: The answer holds every texture slug; the files of one texture are https://api.polyhaven.com/files/<slug>. The game takes the handful it needs, not the whole set.

sources.label: Smith's Dictionary of Antiquities, one entry at a time
sources.licence: 1875 text is public domain; Thayer's own notes are his
sources.note: No bulk scrape: one entry per request, added as the game cites it. The folder name holds a literal star (SMIGRA*), so the url keeps it. An entry that answers 404 is reported and left out, never faked.

sources.label: Wikimedia Commons Latin pronunciation audio
sources.licence: per file, as the file page states
sources.note: The answer holds every ogg url and its licence, so the voice of a legion can carry the licence with it.
